description: Engineering and CS students focused on software development, ML, and data processing. We build robust end-to-end prototypes using open NASA datasets, combining clean system architecture with data visualization to solve real-world space challenges.
summary: Triton Wildfire is a real-time, bilingual (EN/RU) geospatial analytics web application that harmonizes multi-decadal NASA MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) active fire hotspot records into a unified burning activity calendar and 1x1 km fire cluster grid. Because a single 1 km2 wildfire footprint covers 7.11 VIIRS sub-pixels, raw VIIRS streams split single fires into multiple fragmented detections, flooding emergency dispatchers with duplicate alarms and creating artificial post-2012 surges in historical fire trends. Our 4-stage pure-physics pipeline (Triton Engine v2.1) filters sub-threshold smoldering noise (< 3.0 MW), performs spherical Haversine geodesic clustering with off-nadir bowtie scan-overlap suppression and multi-pass normalization, calibrates Fire Radiative Power (FRP) independently from VIIRS data (R2 = 0.9965 across 5 ecosystems in Kazakhstan), and masks industrial gas flares. The platform provides early warning, historical trend analysis (2002-2026), and one-click GeoJSON/CSV export for emergency responders.
